subject.title: [Feature]: sessions_kill should terminate all child exec processes spawned by a session

question: What public session exec-control contract and authorization boundary should OpenClaw expose for listing and terminating child exec processes spawned by a stored session?
rationale: The missing behavior is clear, but exposing session-wide process visibility and termination can cross agent/session boundaries and must be a deliberate product and security boundary choice before a repair worker wires it into Gateway and CLI surfaces.

options.title: Add guarded session exec-control surface
options.body: Create new additive Gateway/CLI methods for session exec list and kill with explicit operator scope, canonical session resolution, per-run outcomes, and tests for child, PTY, sandbox, and fallback behavior.

options.title: Extend existing abort/delete semantics
options.body: Add explicit opt-in flags to existing session maintenance methods, preserving current defaults while documenting the stronger kill semantics and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Defer public operator surface
options.body: Keep the existing agent-scoped process tool only and track orphan/restart cleanup in narrower lifecycle issues until a broader process-control design is ready.

recommendation.title: Add guarded session exec-control surface
recommendation.body: Create new additive Gateway/CLI methods for session exec list and kill with explicit operator scope, canonical session resolution, per-run outcomes, and tests for child, PTY, sandbox, and fallback behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has recent history across the process supervisor and session/Gateway surfaces and is already mentioned on this issue timeline.
